findings: The upper-right hero graphic is a soft dark smoke/particle gradient that reads as atmospheric garnish; only its thematic tie to Chladni sand patterns keeps it from being generic decoration.
Body copy runs quite small and dense across several sections, risking a wall-of-text feel where the editorial rhythm nearly flattens into uniform gray blocks.
The dark waveform/diagram panels repeat a similar black-box treatment multiple times, edging toward a predictable module rhythm by mid-scroll.
what_works: Ragged left-aligned display serif hero with italic accents ('no hand', 'here') set against an asymmetric dark smoke field — a decisive, non-centered composition no SaaS template reaches for.
Consistent mono utility labels ('IN RESONANCE', section subtitles) playing marginalia against the high-contrast editorial serif — a genuine two-voice typographic system.
The 'Sounding Log' numbered data table with a lone rust-red 'X' row is a real editorial signature, treating the page as an instrument log rather than a landing page.
Warm cream/charcoal palette with a single muted rust accent used sparingly — restrained named harmony, no purple-gradient default.
A.reasoning: This is clearly not SaaS slop: the hero is an asymmetric ragged serif composition over a themed dark field, and the whole page behaves as a long-form editorial instrument log with a consistent serif-plus-mono two-voice system and a restrained warm palette punctuated by one rust accent. The decisive moves — the numbered 'Sounding Log' with its single red row, the marginalia labeling, the interactive-looking resonance diagrams — are things a templated generator would not produce. It loses points for a somewhat generic atmospheric smoke graphic and dense small body text that occasionally flattens the rhythm, but it clears the bar.

findings: dense justified body text in long unbroken columns creates visual fatigue rather than rhythmic reading
interactive canvases sit in identical black frames with identical caption styling, producing template repetition
left vertical nav is present but its weight and spacing feel ad-hoc against the main text measure
hero typography uses a single editorial voice with only one red accent; no second voice or scale tension
what_works: opening three-line stanza with the single red word creates immediate focal pull
monochrome palette with restrained red and orange labels avoids gradient slop
B.reasoning: Desktop render avoids every cardinal SaaS template shape and uses editorial typography plus integrated interactive figures, yet the layout remains safe in its symmetry of section blocks and lacks a decisive compositional risk or modular spacing system that would lift it above competent literary site defaults.
